scope: Local comparison of the reports database suite's destructive schema fixture; not a production performance or full-suite baseline claim.

runtime.guard: Disposable ppo_synthetic_test database on loopback port 55442 only

measurement.method: Sample active schema-reset query ages, backend identities and blocking PID counts from PostgreSQL activity statistics. Combine continuation logs by backend identity and query start before counting attempts.
measurement.age_definition: Maximum sampled active query age for each observed reset. Idle backend time is excluded. Query age can continue through timeout cleanup, so values above the statement limit are not successful reset durations. Successful query ages are sampled lower bounds rather than exact elapsed times.
measurement.limits: One sequential local comparison. Sampling can miss short queries or transient contention between samples. The observer does not identify PostgreSQL internal cache or catalogue mechanisms. Private raw activity rows, SQL, connection strings and environment files are excluded.

unchanged_main.result: Diagnostic stopped after reproducing schema-reset statement timeouts; no completed baseline suite result is claimed.

fresh_pool_control.source_hash_basis: Exact file bytes used by the completed control run, including the uncommitted fixture change at execution time.
fresh_pool_control.fixture: Await closeDatabase() before reset() for each case. Closing waits for checked-out clients; business assertions and application SQL timeout remain unchanged.

conclusion: Unchanged main reproduced the schema-reset failure while one backend handled repeated resets. The control completed all 42 report cases with a fresh pool per fixture and no observed late reset-cost growth. This supports the narrow test-fixture change without changing application timeouts, transaction logic or report assertions; it does not establish an internal PostgreSQL cause.
